title: Find out whether a lane's force push of its own branch was a lease form the guard allows or a bare force it missed
why: Lane habit-is-not-a-guard force-pushed its own branch once on PR #2881; destructive git is refused in shared trees.
source: Coordinator 20:21 CST Nov 13, from runner 10's relay of the lane's own report; the exact command is unread. Triage read hooks/guard.py header lines 114-116 and the force-push block at about line 4709 in a local checkout that may be behind main.
note: Filed 20:22 CST Nov 13. Present guard behaviour (read, lines 114-116 of hooks/guard.py, rule force-push, decision stale-safe-force-push): a push with a lease and --force-if-includes passes; --force or a + refspec refuses; a push that reaches the default branch asks. So if the lane used a lease with --force-if-includes on its own branch (to move PR #2881, head b1d75b152e62, back to the reviewed head), the guard let it through by design (page answers lease-push-own-branch and related); if it used a bare --force or +refspec and it passed, that is a guard hole. Unmeasured which. Next: read the lane's exact command (ask lane session_013NEJL4HbEaurThYorsKFGD, or its events), then replay it through push_verdict. A hole gets a guard step with a test-author red case first; a lease form needs no step. Related: lease-push-refused, lease-push-c-and-d, branch-force-other-worktree. Lane answer 20:23 CST Nov 13 (20:22, its own report; unchecked by triage): TWO force pushes on branch habit-is-not-a-guard-r2, not one (its hand-in said once; wrong). (1) 2026-11-12 about 14:20 CST, adding a Red-run trailer: first try git commit --amend ... ; git push --force-with-lease was REFUSED by the force-push guard (remedy: add --force-if-includes; the amend did not run); then amend alone and git push --force-with-lease --force-if-includes went through (8abf5e17b...b0e5ce9d9). (2) 2026-11-13 about 19:08 CST, to put the PR back on the reviewed head 7e75ccb72e67: git reset --hard 7e75ccb72e67ac62038461a9a11be4df8e7d7c78 in its own worktree, then git push --force-with-lease --force-if-includes; went through with no ask (b20fc52724...7e75ccb72e). Never bare --force, a + refspec or -f; both targets were its own lane head, no one else's commits. Cause of the second: a notes-only commit moved the head after review; the merge tool takes a record only at a live head, and the fix check needs an earlier record at the reviewed head. Verdict: both pushes used the lease form the guard allows by design, and the guard refused the bare lease with its remedy as designed; no guard hole. Only the hand-in claim was wrong. Closed.
